architecture_decisions.recommendation: Modified union type handling in codegen backend to process all union members instead of just the first one
architecture_decisions.rationale: The original implementation only checked the first nested type in a union and returned early, causing runtime TypeErrors when None values were encountered in optional nested fields (e.g., Optional[NestedModel]). The fix ensures all union members are properly checked with isinstance guards.
alternatives_considered: Adding special handling only for Optional types
Using a different control flow structure like match/case (Python 3.10+)
Modifying the type inference system to detect optional nested fields earlier

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added a final else clause to handle cases that don't match any specific type checks
architecture_decisions.rationale: For unions like Optional[NestedModel], None values need to pass through unchanged. The else clause ensures that when a value doesn't match any of the nested type checks (e.g., it's None), it's assigned directly without attempting field transfer operations that would fail.
alternatives_considered: Adding explicit None checks before the loop
Using a default case in the conditional chain
Catching TypeErrors during field transfer and falling back

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added comprehensive test case for optional nested fields with None values
architecture_decisions.rationale: The test ensures the fix works correctly by creating a dataclass with an optional nested field set to None, encoding it through the DTO backend, and verifying that the None value is preserved in the output. This prevents regression and matches the non-codegen backend's behavior.
alternatives_considered: Only testing with the codegen backend
Adding the test to a different test file
Creating more complex test scenarios with multiple optional levels

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Maintained existing code generation patterns while fixing the control flow logic
architecture_decisions.rationale: The change preserves the same function signature and overall structure of _handle_transfer_instance, only modifying the loop logic and adding the else block. This ensures existing generated code continues to work while fixing the specific issue with optional nested fields.
alternatives_considered: Refactoring the entire function for clarity
Creating a separate handler for union types
Changing the API of the codegen backend

tickets.title: Fix union type handling in DTO codegen backend
tickets.description: Update the code generation logic to properly handle all members of union types, particularly Optional[NestedModel] patterns where None values were causing runtime errors

tickets.title: Add test coverage for optional nested field encoding
tickets.description: Create test case to verify that models with optional nested fields set to None can be encoded without errors and preserve the None value in output

implementation_summary:
The implementation addresses a critical bug in the DTO code generation backend where optional nested fields in unions were not properly handled. The original code in `_handle_transfer_instance` only processed the first nested type in a union and returned early, causing runtime TypeErrors when None values were encountered in patterns like Optional[NestedModel].

The fix modifies the control flow to generate isinstance checks for all nested types within the union using a conditional chain (if/elif). A key addition is the final else clause that handles cases where the value doesn't match any specific type check—such as None in an Optional type. This ensures None values pass through unchanged without attempting field transfer operations that would fail.

The changes integrate seamlessly with the existing codebase by maintaining the same function signature and code generation patterns. The added test case creates dataclasses with optional nested fields, encodes them through both backends, and verifies that None values are preserved. This ensures the codegen backend now matches the behavior of the non-codegen backend and maintains backward compatibility with existing DTO configurations.
